event: Nala tells the woman she is listening to what is better than coin.
The woman's smile opens enough to show the edge of her teeth.
She sits up on the cutting table beside the silk, boots swinging clear of the floor.
The silk slides with her, turning green where it folds and grey again as it settles.
She tells Nala she is of the Spring Court, as the still-bolted door will have shown.
Her bargain: Nala makes her a gown from this silk with her own hands, done by moonrise on Beltane.
If Nala does it, Nala may ask her for one thing.
If it is not done by moonrise, Nala owes the Spring Court a year of sewing across the ford.
She wets her thumb and holds it out to Nala, as a bargain is struck at the cattle market.
